rows.claim: Fresh coverage omits legacy chunk/NL addresses
rows.evidence: New admission and one-use eligibility precede candidate writes; ordinary file/URL callers generate new GUIDs and directory callers new ULIDs, while failed retries are excluded. No real producer path reusing a historical orphan identity was demonstrated. Settle with an owned scheduler/workflow reuse reproducer and surviving-key end-state.

rows.claim: Existing provenance bypasses candidate tombstone check
rows.evidence: Candidate retention adds no coverage when provenance already exists. SourcePublicationVisibility.Stage checks the permanent unit tombstone before every content write and returns refusal; retaining an obligation does not revive data or waive that fence.

rows.claim: Malformed fresh workflow markers grant authority
rows.evidence: Initialization additionally requires a matching valid inventory workflow with no retained candidate or FailedRetryMemoryUnitId. IngestionIdentityGuard bounds entry IDs; blank/oversized/orphaned/consumed markers cannot satisfy that eligibility predicate. The snapshot size and marker count are bounded.

rows.claim: Native proof and digest checks establish presence only
rows.evidence: ReadWorkloadStreamAsync deserializes; the helper compares event bytes but does not reconstruct the native proof chain. The existing SDK AuthoritativeEventStreamReader(requireNativeProof:true) supplies that validation without a new platform contract. Stable invalid proof/digest mutations need consumer controls.

rows.claim: PID replacement before first child identity read
rows.evidence: The children list has no birth identity and the first identity read does not check parent membership. This ordering predates the change; the real namespace control changes identity during comm instead. Settle an owned foreign-parent replacement between children enumeration and the first birth read before adding a relationship protocol.

The new shell is started and child output is read/opened before the cleanup try block. A canceled or malformed read can bypass explicit owned cleanup. Own the shell immediately and retain early-failure controls.

rows.claim: Canceled cleanup can skip remaining owned processes
rows.evidence: The procfs reproducer reuses the test token and awaits child exit before attempting parent cleanup. A canceled token or first cleanup failure can skip parent cleanup. Use a fresh bounded cleanup lifetime and attempt every owned process while preserving failures.

rows.claim: Synchronous process waits can hang reproducers
rows.evidence: Both reproducers use synchronous WaitForExit without a timeout; the empty-task fact has no outer timeout. Replace these waits with bounded owned waits/forced cleanup and retain the real passing controls.

rows.claim: Linux namespace prerequisites may be unavailable
rows.evidence: README explicitly declares Linux procfs/user-PID namespace support and the actual host passed. Whether the maintained CI/default supported developer lane schedules this test on a host lacking those prerequisites is unproved. Settle with that lane capability audit and an actual refusal before changing qualification selection.

rows.claim: Typed diagnostics can exceed cooperative capture cancellation
rows.evidence: A call already in flight can finish up to its fixed four-second RPC timeout after capture cancellation. CaptureNativeRefusalAsync deliberately awaits actual cleanup; this is a bounded diagnostic-only delay on a rare failed-read path, not accepted authority or detached work. A linked transport/deadline mechanism exceeds a direct correction for negligible harm.

rows.claim: Fresh provenance and orphan historical chunks
rows.evidence: Same unproved producer-identity reuse boundary as BH1; current admission proof is not inferred solely from base-key absence. A real legacy orphan collision through the scheduler/workflow and surviving deletion end-state would settle it.

rows.claim: Empty native UI provenance is accepted
rows.evidence: record iterates provenance rows without requiring a valid absolute-path/hash row; bind_native_ui only requires the manifest to be inventoried. Empty or metadata-only manifests can therefore satisfy the new wrapper binding. Require source rows during recording and readback, retaining metadata headers.

rows.claim: Early cancellation/malformed output leaves owned child
rows.evidence: Same early ownership boundary as BH6: child output acquisition occurs before the cleanup try block. Own the shell immediately and cover cancellation/malformed-output cleanup.

rows.claim: Stale control actually sends a future epoch
rows.evidence: OwnedRouteCatalogBindingHandler sends state.Epoch+1. This proves noncurrent generation refusal, not the claimed preceding epoch. Send an older epoch in stale mode and retain actual sent versus observed epoch evidence.

rows.claim: Retained launcher mismatch lacks regression coverage
rows.evidence: Pre-verified gap: existing complete-root tests match retained/current starts, and existing churn tests change children later. Add the complete replacement-root case so removing the expected launcher start argument fails the regression.

rows.claim: Child marker alone selects PID allocator mutation
rows.evidence: The namespace reproducer trusts PARTIES_PROCESS_PID_REUSE_CHILD=1 before writing ns_last_pid. A direct/inherited-marker rerun outside the owned namespace reaches that mutation. Verify owned new PID/user namespace identity before starting the mutation branch and test refusal without mutating the host counter.
